question.prompt: Let \(p,\) \(q,\) and \(r\) be the distinct roots of the polynomial \[x^3 - 22x^2 + 80x - 67.\] There exist real numbers \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) such that \[ \begin{gathered} \frac{1}{s^3-22s^2+80s-67}\\ =\frac{A}{s-p}+\frac{B}{s-q}\\ \quad+\frac{C}{s-r} \end{gathered} \] for all real numbers \(s\) with \(s\notin\{p,q,r\}.\) What is \[\dfrac1A+\dfrac1B+\dfrac1C?\]

solutions.title: Substitute roots after clearing denominators
solutions.explanation:
Clearing denominators lets us substitute the roots and isolate one coefficient at a time, without finding the roots themselves.

Because the polynomial is monic with roots \(p,q,r\), its factorization is \((s-p)(s-q)(s-r)\). Multiplying the given equality by this product gives
\[
1=A(s-q)(s-r)+B(s-p)(s-r)+C(s-p)(s-q).
\]
This equality holds for infinitely many values of \(s\), so it is a polynomial identity and holds at the roots as well. Indeed, a nonzero polynomial cannot have infinitely many roots.

Substituting \(s=p\) gives \(1=A(p-q)(p-r)\). Similarly,
\[
\frac1A=(p-q)(p-r),\qquad
\frac1B=(q-p)(q-r),\qquad
\frac1C=(r-p)(r-q).
\]
The roots are distinct, so these products are nonzero. Expanding and collecting terms now yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac1A+\frac1B+\frac1C
&=p^2+q^2+r^2-(pq+pr+qr)\\
&=(p+q+r)^2-3(pq+pr+qr).
\end{aligned}
\]
By Viète's formulas, comparing the coefficients of \(x^2\) and \(x\) gives
\[
p+q+r=22,\qquad pq+pr+qr=80.
\]
Therefore the requested value is
\[
22^2-3\cdot80=484-240=\boxed{244}.
\]
The answer is \(\textbf{(B)}\).
